references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, cities of refuge are mentioned for someone who kills another by accident and without intent.
Describes an example of unintentional killing without enmity, where a man accidentally kills his neighbor while they are chopping wood together.
Refers to cases where God allows something to happen even though the perpetrator had no intention to kill, and that there should be a place of refuge.
Describes the purpose of the cities of refuge for someone who kills another by accident and without intent, so that he may flee there.
The continuation of the verse that clarifies what is meant by unintentional killing without enmity or evil intent.
